{
  "problem_addressed": "Developing an infrared and collinear (IRC) safe jet clustering algorithm that possesses the 'soft-resilient' boundary properties of iterative cone algorithms (circular jets unaffected by soft radiation) without inheriting their collinear unsafety.",
  "methodology": "The authors propose the 'anti-kt' algorithm, a member of a generalized class of sequential recombination algorithms defined by the distance measures dij = min(kti^{2p}, ktj^{2p}) * (Δij^2 / R^2) and diB = kti^{2p}. By setting p = -1, the algorithm ensures that hard particles act as centers for clustering soft particles, creating conical jets with radius R, whereas soft particles only cluster among themselves after interacting with hard ones.",
  "experiments": "The algorithm was evaluated through: 1) Analytical study of jet areas (passive and active) and anomalous dimensions. 2) Simulation of dijet events at the LHC using Pythia 6.4 and Herwig 6.5 to analyze area distributions, fluctuations, and 'back-reaction' effects. 3) Testing top mass reconstruction in ttbar events simulated with Pythia 6.4 using a standard selection and pairing procedure.",
  "results": "The anti-kt algorithm produces jets that are nearly perfectly circular with area πR², showing almost zero area fluctuations and vanishing anomalous dimensions (d = 0, D = 0). It exhibits significantly suppressed 'back-reaction' compared to kt, Cambridge/Aachen, and SISCone. Theoretically, it shares the non-global logarithm structure of ideal cones and maintains a universal Milan factor. In top mass reconstruction tests, it performed similarly to or marginally better than other IRC-safe algorithms.",
  "limitations": "Computational complexity is asymptotically O(N^(3/2)) for p < 0 in worst-case scenarios for Voronoi-based implementations, although practically efficient for N < 20,000 via FastJet.",
  "future_work": "Investigation of less negative values of p to explore trade-offs between soft-resilience and adaptability to harder substructure.",
  "main_contributions": [
    "Introduction of the anti-kt jet clustering algorithm as an IRC-safe replacement for iterative cone algorithms.",
    "Demonstration that anti-kt jets possess soft-resilient boundaries, leading to regular conical shapes.",
    "Proof that anti-kt eliminates area anomalous dimensions and minimizes back-reaction from pileup/underlying events."
  ],
